BIOET 100: This course surveys core topics in recent bioethics - the study of ethical problems issuing from the use and treatment of human and non-human animals in the research and practice of medicine and biotechnology.
BIOET 110N: This survey course explores the human experience of health and illness from a combined social/behavioral science and humanities perspective.
BIOET 220N: This inter-domain (GH and GS) course will introduce students to the application of technology-ethics and bioethics, as well as the humanities (especially health and medical humanities) and the social sciences, through the lens of science fiction and speculative fiction.
BIOET 322: The course explores how emerging technologies impact beliefs, practices, research, and communication regarding the nature of knowledge, learning, teaching, remix culture, visuality, materiality, self, and art.
BIOET 401Q: This course explores the ethical, policy, and legal implications of science, and the implications of science for ethics, policy, and law.
BIOET 432: This course examines ethical, social, legal, and policy issues related to the research, implementation, and practice of medicine, medical technologies, and healthcare.
BIOET 496: Creative projects, including research and design, which are supervised on an individual basis and which fall outside the scope of formal courses.
BIOET 497: Creative projects, including research and design, which are supervised on an individual basis and which fall outside the scope of formal courses.
